# Data report presentation scenario

Use this scenario for KPI reviews, research findings, operational analysis,
experiments, surveys, or evidence-led recommendations.

- Working title: <presentation title>
- Audience: <decision-makers or analysts>
- Question to answer: <one analytical question>
- Decision or action enabled: <outcome>
- Analysis period: <date range>
- Data sources: <systems, files, studies>
- Target slide count: <count or range>

## Scenario arc

| Stage | Audience question | Assertion to establish | Required evidence | Transition to next stage | Suggested slides |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Question | What decision-relevant question does the analysis answer? | <the question and success measure are unambiguous> | <business context, metric definition> | Explain whether the data can answer it credibly | 1 |
| Method | How reliable and comparable is the analysis? | <scope, source, sample, and method support the conclusion> | <definitions, coverage, exclusions> | Present the most decision-relevant findings first | 1 |
| Finding | What changed or differs materially? | <one quantified finding per slide> | <chart, table, confidence, baseline> | Move from observation to explanation | 2–4 |
| Interpretation | Why did it happen and what uncertainty remains? | <drivers and limitations explain the finding without overstating causality> | <segmentation, comparison, caveats> | Translate the finding into impact | 1–2 |
| Impact | Why does the result matter? | <finding changes cost, risk, experience, or opportunity> | <scenario, forecast, affected population> | Compare available responses | 1–2 |
| Recommendation | What action follows from the evidence? | <recommended action is proportional to evidence and uncertainty> | <options, expected effect, cost> | Define measurement and ownership | 1–2 |
| Next measure | How will we know the action worked? | <owner, metric, target, and review date close the loop> | <measurement plan> | End with the required decision or action | 1 |

## Claim and evidence register

| Claim | Metric definition | Source | Analysis period | Confidence | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <claim> | <numerator, denominator, unit> | <source> | <period> | High / Medium / Low | <limitation> |

## Analytical integrity checks

- Baseline and comparison periods: <definitions>
- Population, sample, and exclusions: <definitions>
- Missing data and outliers: <treatment>
- Correlation versus causation: <allowed conclusion>
- Statistical or practical significance: <threshold>
- Reproducibility: <query, notebook, report, owner>

## Scenario acceptance checks

- The analytical question and metric definitions precede the findings.
- Each finding slide states one quantified conclusion, unit, period, and source.
- Limitations and uncertainty appear before recommendations.
- Recommendations are proportional to the strength of the evidence.
- The final stage assigns an action, metric, owner, and review date.
